Shadow verified on all three coins: correct token per side vs gamma, exact dollar math, caps respected; btc's clean hour showed 243 signals with zero pricing-integrity rejections. risk._micro_note: Two live strategies on a ~$68 wallet. The risk block is GLOBAL, not per-strategy, so this sizes the COMBINED book: 3 concurrent x $12 = $36 worst-case committed, about half the bankroll, with the rest as settlement buffer. They rarely collide -- jumpscalp fires in a market's first 5s and is flat within 30s; rollavg fires in its last 30s. Daily stop $20: jumpscalp alone runs ~63 trades/day at 20sh, so a normal day swings roughly +/-$13 around an expected +$26 -- a tighter stop would fire on noise, a looser one is a third of the wallet.

rollavg_edge._disabled_note: OFF as of 2026-08-20: the endgame taker is retired from live. Micro-live measured its structural problem directly -- adverse fill selection (171 kills vs 14 fills; fills avg px 0.296 vs paper 0.857) -- and the filtered variant traded too rarely to pay for its tail risks. EarlyBird replaces it as the sole real-money strategy: same model, opposite end of the window, where the book is two-sided and the strike is already formed. Retiring it also frees both concurrency slots for consecutive EarlyBird holds and removes the endgame-only failure paths (concurrent unknown resolutions on one token, post-drop orphan fills). The paper bot keeps the unfiltered endgame as the frozen control for live_vs_paper.
rollavg_edge._size_note: 10 shares (~$9 at typical fill px) against paper's 100. Every GATE is identical to the frozen paper config -- same zmin, same max_price, same window -- so live and paper disagree only about execution, which is the one thing micro-live exists to measure. The venue min is 5 shares; risk room below that is logged as live_miss/below_venue_min, not sent.
rollavg_edge._require_edge_note: ON for LIVE as of 2026-08-20 (paper keeps it OFF as the control). Live measured adverse fill selection the tape cannot show: 171 kills vs 14 fills overnight, with fills averaging px 0.296 vs paper's 0.857 -- the venue fills us eagerly when the quote is going bad and starves us when it's right. require_edge only buys when ask <= empirical_fair - edge_min (2c), the pre-measured +10.15c/sh filter (3x per-share edge on ~1/5 volume): trades that are mispriced in OUR favor, which adverse selection cannot punish. The divergence report A/Bs this against the unfiltered paper baseline.
rollavg_edge._relaunch_note: RE-ENABLED 2026-08-21 with the padded marketable limit. It was retired on 08-20 for adverse fill selection; that turned out to be an EXECUTION defect (unpadded limit + a round() that put the limit UNDER the ask above 0.96), not a defect of the prediction. Print-proof pooled: +5.51c/sh t=3.02, 7/9 days positive, holdout Aug18-21 +4.44c/sh; ~25 trades/day at the current micro caps. Entries skew cheap (avg 0.213) so per-trade variance is high: the daily stop, not the per-trade size, is the real risk control.
rollavg_edge._gate_note: PAPER gate, unchanged: require_edge false, max_price 0.99, zmin 2.0. This is the configuration to fix and measure, not to redesign. It was briefly switched to require_edge after four live trades lost -- a 4-fill sample against a 628-fill measurement (+3.24c/sh, t=2.99, 8/9 days positive) on a strategy whose per-share sd is 34c. That override was not justified by the evidence and is reverted. Capacity note: the deep book sits at 0.96-0.99 (10k+ shares resting, book probe median depth 33,767), which is exactly the band this gate trades, so size is limited by the edge holding at scale, not by liquidity.

_latency_note: Used by the paper half of shadow mode only. In live mode no simulated latency is added: the venue's real 250ms hold and the real Amsterdam rtt replace the model.
_fill_note: Drives the paper simulation inside shadow mode and min_order_size (the venue's orderMinSize) in live mode. The rest is ignored by the live path: reality fills real orders.

zmaker._note: MEASUREMENT ONLY -- simulated against real trade prints in an isolated ledger (maker_fills.jsonl / maker_sim_settled lines), never touching the real-money broker or risk. Rationale: 24h of live takers measured adverse fill selection (171 kills vs 14 fills; fills at avg 0.296 vs paper 0.857) -- the favourite's ask side empties in the final 30s, so the taker leg starves where the edge is largest. The maker leg rests a bid at fair-minus-3c on the favoured side, TTL 10s, cancel-and-replace, never resting into the final 3s. Maker fills on prints are the HONEST direction of simulation (prints are executed volume). If a few days measure it positive at meaningful volume, the real maker executor gets built.

_taker_pad_note: Marketable-limit padding: the fix for one-way fill selection. A CLOB fills a taker at the RESTING maker's price and this venue re-validates after its 250ms taker hold, so a limit set to exactly the ask we saw dies to any uptick in flight -- meaning we filled when the price fell (wrong) and were killed when it rose (right). Measured live: 171 kills / 14 fills, fills avg 0.296 vs paper 0.857. Padding pays the ask when the book is unchanged and still matches when it moved, Bounded three ways: relative to price (taker_pad_rel, so a flat 5c cannot become a 167% overpay on a 3c ask), absolutely (taker_pad), and by value (paying the limit in full must still leave taker_pad_min_edge after fee). Sizing runs on the PADDED limit because a BUY here is rate-based -- size x limit is the cash committed -- so the per-market dollar cap binds on money that can actually leave. Print-proof measurement, 6788 markets x 3 coins x 9 days: fill rate 68->89% (btc), 44->67% (eth), 33->54% (sol); pooled deployed gate +3.37c/sh t=1.75 -> +5.51c/sh t=3.02.
_probe_note: Probe config: identical gate and padding to config.live.json, sized so an hour of real orders answers the fill question for a few dollars. Graduate to config.live.json sizing only after the measured kill:fill ratio beats 5:1.
_desync_note: Blocks a signal whose price disagrees with the venue's OWN last print by more than this. Replaces a model-disagreement check that silently halved the strategy: calib.py's p_up spans [0.1833, 0.9159], so a Down contract can never be valued above 0.8167 and every Down favourite at 0.97-0.99 scored ev -0.17 and was blocked, while the identical Up trade at -0.075 passed. Measured live: 10 blocks, all Down. The guard's real job is a frozen book view (launch day: ours stuck at 0.99 while the venue traded 0.022), which a print comparison catches directly.

jumpscalp._note: Trade the opening jump, never the outcome: buy near 0.50 in the first seconds, leave inside 30s at +9c or flat. Out-of-sample btc (5 days the parameters never saw): taker exit +2.07c/sh t=4.37, maker +2.82c/sh t=5.75, 6/6 days positive, survives dropping the 20 best trades, bootstrap P(EV<=0)=0.0000. In-sample was WEAKER (+1.00c taker), so the rule did not degrade out of sample. Exits are marketable FAK limits, never resting orders -- the +2.07c figure assumes no queue position, and a rested sell is what made ZMaker lose 22.8c/sh. NOT ESTABLISHED: eth (+0.71c) and sol (-0.06c) show nothing out-of-sample; btc only until that is understood. Scaling: entry depth p10 is 54sh so past ~250sh the book gets walked and ~1c of slippage takes half a 2c edge -- confident zone is 50-100sh.
